reception: Reception of the correspondence itself is small but concrete. The citations that engage it come from tools: a framework for characterizing segmental duplication structure across genome assemblies is written in Seq, Sequre builds secure multiparty computation for biomedical data sharing on top of it, and Vectron uses its infrastructure for auto-vectorized dynamic programming. Other genomics work, including minimizer-space assembly and the mapquik read mapper, cites it when arguing that performance-minded tooling matters in the field. Much of the small external record is unjudged, so the fuller picture is uncertain, but the judged citations are the kind a language wants: people writing software in it. The language lives on at seq-lang/seq and, under the Codon umbrella, at exaloop/seq.
